title: Official Visit of Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas, to Mauritius
subtitle: Agreements signed to power Mauritius energy security
body_text:
Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, made an official visit to the Republic of Mauritius from 20-21 August 2026.
On August 20, Minister called on His Excellency Dr. Navinchandra Ramgoolam, Prime Minister of Mauritius. In their presence, India and Mauritius exchanged a Government-to-Government (G2G) Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for cooperation in Oil and Gas sector, alongside a long-term Sales and Purchase agreement between Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) and the State Trading Corporation (STC) of Mauritius for supply of petroleum products. Under the Agreement, IOCL will supply the entire import requirement of Mauritius of Motor Spirit (MS), High Speed Diesel (HSD) and Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF).
The MoU on oil and gas cooperation institutionalises the longstanding energy partnership between the two countries, covering petroleum products supply, training and capacity building for Mauritian officials and biofuels cooperation. The five-year agreement between IOCL and STC is an assured long-term supply commitment to Mauritius, providing the country with security of supplies and shielding it from price volatility. This is the first long-term supply agreement concluded by an Indian PSU Oil Marketing Company outside South Asia in recent years.
During the visit, Minister also held productive bilateral meetings with Hon’ble Patrick Gervais Assirvaden, Minister of Energy and Public Utilities, Hon’ble John Michaël Tzoun Sao Yeung Sik Yuen, Minister of Commerce and Consumer Protection and Hon’ble Dhananjay Ramful and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Integration and International Trade. He participated in a ground breaking ceremony of India Oil (Mauritius) Ltd’s 27.5 TMT bunker marine fuel storage facility at Mer Rouge, Port Louis.
India's growing role as a dependable energy partner
India has emerged as a major global refining hub, with an annual output of 267 MMT of refined petroleum products across 23 refineries, making it a net exporter of refined products. India already meets the petroleum demand of Nepal and Bhutan and supplies significant quantities to other countries in the region and beyond. Even during the ongoing West Asia crisis, India has fulfilled its supply commitments to Nepal and Bhutan, making it a dependable energy security provider for the region. The agreement with Mauritius positions India as the country's anchor fuel supplier and strengthens India's strategic and economic footprint in the Indian Ocean region.
MoU also extends cooperation in biofuels
The MoU further provides for cooperation in biofuels through exchange of knowledge, research and training. Mauritius is a founding member of the Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA), an initiative piloted by India and launched during India's G20 Presidency. As part of its country engagement programme, the GBA Secretariat has partnered with Mauritius' Ministry of Energy and Public Utilities in developing a Biofuels Country Landscape Policy framework for the country.
Minister Puri and Hon’ble Patrick Gervais Assirvaden jointly witnessed the launch of the Biofuels Country Landscape Policy framework on August 21, marking a starting point for Mauritius in exploring its energy transition through biofuels.

enrichment.summary: Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri visited Mauritius on 20-21 August 2026, during which India and Mauritius signed a Government-to-Government MoU on oil and gas cooperation and a five-year Sales and Purchase Agreement between IOCL and Mauritius's State Trading Corporation, under which IOCL will meet Mauritius's entire import requirement of petrol, diesel and aviation fuel. This is the first long-term supply agreement by an Indian PSU oil marketing company outside South Asia in recent years. The visit also saw the launch of a Biofuels Country Landscape Policy framework for Mauritius under the India-led Global Biofuels Alliance, and groundbreaking for a bunker marine fuel storage facility by Indian Oil (Mauritius) Ltd.
enrichment.context:
India has been positioning itself as a reliable regional energy security provider, already supplying the entire petroleum demand of landlocked neighbours Nepal and Bhutan and maintaining these commitments even during the ongoing West Asia crisis. With 23 refineries producing 267 MMT annually, India is a net exporter of refined petroleum products and is now extending this role into the Indian Ocean Region, where it competes for strategic influence with China. The Mauritius agreement is significant because it marks India's first long-term OMC supply deal outside South Asia, extending its energy diplomacy beyond the subcontinent and reinforcing its 'SAGAR' (Security and Growth for All in the Region) vision and broader Indian Ocean strategic footprint.

The biofuels component connects to the Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA), launched during India's G20 Presidency in 2023 to promote biofuel adoption, trade and technology sharing globally. Mauritius, a founding GBA member, is now developing a national biofuels policy framework with GBA Secretariat support, illustrating how India uses multilateral platforms it initiated to deepen bilateral energy partnerships and support small island nations' energy transitions.

prelims_questions.question: The Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA), mentioned in the context of India-Mauritius biofuels cooperation, was launched during which event?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that Mauritius is a founding member of the Global Biofuels Alliance, an initiative piloted by India and launched during India's G20 Presidency.

prelims_questions.question: As per the release, which Indian Oil Marketing Company signed a long-term Sales and Purchase Agreement with Mauritius's State Trading Corporation for supply of petroleum products?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifies that IOCL signed the long-term agreement with STC of Mauritius to supply the entire import requirement of MS, HSD and ATF.

mains_questions.question: Discuss how India's growing refining capacity and long-term fuel supply agreements with countries like Nepal, Bhutan and now Mauritius are shaping its energy diplomacy and strategic footprint in the Indian Ocean Region.
Examine the role of the Global Biofuels Alliance in advancing India's clean energy diplomacy and assess its significance for small island developing states like Mauritius.

study_notes.reason: The release has a solid factual core (G2G MoU, IOCL-STC agreement, GBA details) that UPSC could test as objective facts, while also offering strong material on India's Indian Ocean energy diplomacy and SAGAR strategy for analytical answers - genuinely dual-use.

prelims.point: IOCL-STC (Mauritius) five-year Sales and Purchase Agreement makes India the sole supplier of Mauritius's entire MS, HSD and ATF import requirement
prelims.why_important: This is the specific factual announcement the release exists to report and could be tested on details like product coverage and duration.

prelims.point: This is the first long-term supply agreement by an Indian PSU Oil Marketing Company outside South Asia in recent years
prelims.why_important: A distinctive superlative fact UPSC often uses in 'first of its kind' statement-based questions.

prelims.point: Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA) was launched during India's G20 Presidency in 2023; Mauritius is a founding member
prelims.why_important: GBA is an India-led multilateral initiative frequently referenced in energy diplomacy questions, and its origin/founding members are testable facts.

prelims.point: India has 23 refineries with annual refined petroleum output of 267 MMT, making it a net exporter of refined products
prelims.why_important: A quantifiable economic fact about India's refining capacity that could appear in data-based prelims questions.

prelims.point: India already meets the entire petroleum demand of Nepal and Bhutan
prelims.why_important: Establishes India's existing regional energy supplier role, useful for distinguishing scope of commitments across neighbours.

prelims.point: SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) is India's strategic vision for the Indian Ocean Region
prelims.why_important: A named policy doctrine frequently tested in prelims on India's foreign policy initiatives and their meanings.

mains.point: The Mauritius agreement extends India's energy diplomacy beyond South Asia into the Indian Ocean Region, reinforcing SAGAR vision and countering China's regional influence
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on India's Indian Ocean Region strategy, SAGAR doctrine, or India-China strategic competition in small island states.

mains.point: India maintained fuel supply commitments to Nepal and Bhutan even during the West Asia crisis, positioning itself as a dependable energy security provider
mains.analytical_use: Deployable in questions on energy security, India's role as a reliable supplier amid global supply disruptions, or resilience of India's refining sector.

mains.point: India uses multilateral platforms it initiated (like GBA) to deepen bilateral energy partnerships and support small island nations' energy transitions
mains.theme: Multilateralism as a tool of bilateral diplomacy
mains.analytical_use: Useful for analysing how India leverages G20-era initiatives for soft power and bilateral leverage, especially with SIDS (Small Island Developing States).

mains.point: Long-term supply agreements shield partner countries from price volatility, strengthening India's soft power and economic leverage in the region
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for discussing instruments of India's economic diplomacy and how energy security assurances build strategic partnerships.

low_priority.reason: Routine diplomatic protocol detail without substantive policy content.
